subject: CoreWorx pricing inquiry — migration & price-equality proposal
messages:
From: Lauren Park <lauren@coreworx.com>

Cc: procurement@coreworx.com
Date: 2027-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + ask: can Redwood match CloudForge economics?

Hi Karthik,

We had a good demo last week — thanks. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of concrete asks so we can include Redwood in the short list for our replacement RFP. CoreWorx is currently under a multi-region contract with CloudForge; procurement wants two things: (1) a clear price-match or superior TCO offering (token/runtime pricing + expected egress/ingress impacts) and (2) a migration package that reduces risk & one-time switching costs.

Can you share a price-match framework and an estimate for an onboarding/migration credit? I attached the CloudForge contract excerpt and our last three months of aggregated usage (summary). Helpful context: avg monthly token usage ~ 320M tokens, 3 active environments (dev/stage/prod), strict SLA for production inference (<250ms p95).

Also flag any dependencies (quota timing, reserved commitment, region capacity).

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Park
VP, Platform Engineering | CoreWorx
lauren@coreworx.com

Attachments: CloudForge_current_terms.pdf (excerpt, redacted), CF_usage_summary_M12023-202702.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Lauren Park <lauren@coreworx.com>
Cc: procurement@coreworx.com
Date: 2027-03-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + ask: can Redwood match CloudForge economics?

Hi Lauren — great to hear from you and thanks for the context + contract excerpt. We can absolutely put together a formal price-match proposal, but to avoid back-and-forth I want to confirm a couple quick things before I model numbers:

- Is the 320M token figure steady-state or includes a recent pilot spike?
- How much of your traffic is latency-sensitive (prod <250ms p95) vs batch/inference queues?
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency, SOC2 type II evidence required)?

High-level we typically approach these requests with: a committed reserved-capacity discount (term-based), a one-time migration credit to cover integration effort and egress, and a short trial pilot with an escalation/fallback SLA. I've attached our standard price-match guarantee doc so you can see the guardrails we apply.

If you can share a short window tomorrow (30m) I'll walk through the high-level model and commit to a draft proposal by EOD Friday.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding the CoreWorx ask. Key signals: 320M avg tokens/month, 3 envs, strict p95 latency. Procurement expects a price-match + migration credit.

My proposed starting point (quick ballpark):
- 12-month reserved commitment at 15% off list for committed baseline (to get unit economics aligned with CloudForge).
- Migration credit equivalent to 2x avg monthly usage (applied as bill credit over first 60 days) to offset egress/integration.
- Optional 3-month pilot (no-commit) with limited throughput and a fast-fail rollback.

Questions for you: what flexibility on discount can we give for a 24-month commitment? And would you accept a migration credit that is conditional on an executed SOW for our PS team (preferred)?

FYI I suggested including optional paid PS hours for the heavier migration items (data export, infra cutover) so we don't eat professional services costs entirely. Thoughts?

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik — good summary. My suggested framework (commercial + guardrails):

1) Term & Discount
- 12-month commitment: 15% off published hosted API list pricing for committed baseline (applies to tokens + embeddings).
- 24-month commitment: 22% off if CoreWorx prepays or commits to reserved Dedicated capacity (we can price reserved nodes separately).

2) Migration Credit
- One-time credit equal to 2x their avg monthly invoice (explicitly limited to invoice credits — does not cover third-party PS).
- Credit paid across first two invoice cycles to reduce churn risk.

3) Technical/Operational Conditions
- Pilot window (30d) with limited token quota; production SLA starts only after go-live acceptance tests.
- Optional paid PS SOW: we offer a discounted PS rate for the first 40 hours to help with exports, KV cache seeding, and cutover automation.

4) Safeguards (legal/finance)
- Credit clawback if they terminate <90d after go-live.
- Egress assumptions: include an estimate for the first TB of egress; if egress >x TB we'd revisit economics.

Attached a quick model I put together (migration_credit_model.xlsx). Numbers to share externally need finance sign-off but this is a working recommendation.

Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: migration_credit_model.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: procurement@coreworx.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-05T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: Redwood tailored price-equality + migration package (draft)

Hi Lauren — appreciate the details and patience. Per our conversation and internal review, here's a formal draft proposal for your procurement committee. Happy to walk through with the team.

SUMMARY (high-level)
- Committed baseline: 12-month term covering standard hosted inference tokens and embeddings. 15% discount off Redwood hosted list pricing for committed baseline (applies to observed 320M tokens/month baseline).
- Migration credit: One-time invoice credit equal to 2x avg monthly invoice (credit applied as two equal credits across first two invoices).
- Pilot: Optional 30-day pilot with a non-binding quota (up to 50M tokens) and acceptance test prior to production SLA start.
- PS assistance: Optional SOW for migration work. We will credit the first 40 hours at a 50% discount if the 12-month term is executed.
- SLA & rollback: Production SLA p95 <250ms for prod cluster; fallback clause to run on CloudForge for 14 days if SLA breach occurs post-go-live (technical rollback costs limited per SOW).

Estimate (illustrative)
- Baseline committed discount saves ~15% on per-token unit cost vs list; with migration credit and PS discount the first-year effective price gap vs CloudForge is expected to be neutral-to-favorable depending on egress. Exact $s require their last 3 months of invoices (we used the token summary provided).

Next steps
1) If this aligns, sign a short mutual NDA so we can exchange full invoices and production SRE contact.
2) Finance will provide a final quote with line-item: list price, committed discount, migration-credit value, PS SOW estimate.
3) Pilot kickoff + runbook review (target pilot start within 2 weeks of SOW).

I've attached a formal PDF proposal and the price-match guardrails we referenced earlier. Please let me know availability for a 30m legal/procurement call on Monday.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
